preview: Aaryan J. Apte shares his interview experience for the internship role at Bank of America, detailing the resume shortlisting, HireVue interview, Group Discussion, and multiple personal interview rounds.
content: Aaryan J. Apte B. Tech, Computer Engineering INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE 30th November 2023 Details: First up: This division of Bank of America visited VJTI for the first time. Eligibility Criteria: CS, IT, EXTC and Electronics students were eligible. There were 2 roles they were offering: 1. Global Banking Technology (Managerial Role). 2. Global Markets Technology (Software Development Role). Both didn’t have a CPI criteria. However, there was a condition of no active backlogs. Stipend: ₹1,41,000 per month. Résumé Shortlisting: It was the usual process of Google Form where we attached our résumés . 1. Make sure that you have your résumé ready well before time. 2. Try your best to make your résumé stand out amongst others. 3. Put everything in points. 4. Keep it crisp and try to fit it on one page. 5. Remember, you should write your resume such that it drives the conversation. Out of 250 students who had applied (130 in Banking and 120 in Development), 120 students were selected for the next round (40 from Banking and 80 from Development). HireVue One-way Interview: 1. I would recommend you to watch these videos: 2. Bank of America HireVue Video Interview Questions and Answers Practice HireVue Video Interview: 5 MISTAKES You Need to AVOID 3. You must have thoughts clear in your mind. 4. Then you just have to re-assemble them during the interview. 5. Most importantly, be absolutely comfortable and relaxed. 6. Remember one thing: ‘They just want to get to know you’. Out of 120 students, 45 students (about 20 in banking and 25 in Development) were shortlisted based on the one-way interview. Group Discussion: On the 28th of November, 6 people from Bank of America visited VJTI for in-person interviews. Batches of 11 were made for the GD. To ensure fairness, all 6 of them were present as judges. My group was given the topic: “Cashless Economy - Success or Failure?”, with 1 minute to prepare the points. 1. Don’t be anxious to start. If no one seems to take the lead, then take the lead. 2. Never be aggressive in a GD. Respect the conflicting views. 3. Always take a firm stand. Even though you may not be correct, do not change your stand on the subject. 4. It is not about who speaks the most, it is more about presenting the reasons behind your views. 5. Have a welcoming body language. Smile often and importantly, be patient. First Interview: Out of the 45 students, 25 students (11 from Banking and 14 from Development) were shortlisted for the personal interview round. The 6 people had split into 3 panels of 2 people each. There was 1 panel for interviewing the students for the Development role and 2 panels for the management role. My panel consisted of the senior-most member who was with BofA for the last 35 years and one other who was with BofA for 15 years. The senior-most person welcomed me. I gave each of them my resume and they asked me to summarize the contents. I thought rather than going directly to the resume, it would be better to let them know who I am as a person. So, I asked them 'Can I start by telling you about myself?’. After talking about myself which lasted for about 4 minutes, the conversation was directed towards “Aaryan… Why did you leave IIT and come to VJTI?” Subsequently, we had a normal discussion where they asked me the reason I wanted to work with Bank of America, my understanding of the role and my future aspirations. Post this, I was selected for the final round (9 people out of 25 were shortlisted for the final round). 1. Keep the conversation lively. 2. If you do not know something, let them know. Do not lie. 3. Again, have your fragments of answers ready. You can stitch them together and deliver a brilliant response when the time comes. 4. Be yourself. It is about helping them understand you and like you as a person. Final Interview: In the final round, I was interviewed by the entire panel. Apart from the questions asked in the previous round, they asked me “Why did you select German to learn?”, “What do you know of Project Management?”, “How will you handle your team’s morale?”. They were very satisfied with my responses. Results: Out of the 9 students, Bank of America offered internships to 4 students, 2 students for Global Markets Technology and 2 students, including me, for Global Banking Technology. 1. There were people who had a stronger resume than mine. However, BofA was the company who gave consideration to the overall personality of the student along with their technical skills. 2. Try to have a well rounded personality, be the one who can communicate very well and speak with conviction and confidence. 3. Most importantly, ‘Dil se baat karo. Dil se nikli baat hi dil tak jaati hai…’
